_comment: ADR-019 decision 1: numeric_environment_hash + accepted_image_digests + build manifest hash.
Text, therefore in git under ADR-014's rules. Concrete digests live here and never in an ADR.
numeric_environment_hash below is MEASURED, from inside the running image, by
`container/build.sh`. It is not a value anyone typed. Two independent builds -- the second
with --no-cache, so a genuine re-resolve rather than a reused layer -- produced BYTE-IDENTICAL
environment documents, and the hash was recomputed from the archived document afterwards.
It is stable because everything it rests on is pinned: the base image by digest, the apt
archive by snapshot timestamp, the interpreter and uv by version, and the dependency set by
uv.lock. Before the lock existed this field could not honestly be filled: two builds a month
apart could have resolved different wheels while the predicate claimed they had not.

note: The Dockerfile's FROM pins index_digest, which is the multi-arch index. The amd64 manifest
it resolves to is recorded alongside it so that a future reader can tell whether a changed
index digest actually changed the amd64 image or only added a platform.
This carries a `sha256:` prefix and that is correct: it is an OCI reference, not a field in
a FarSight hashed document. ADR-001 decision 7's bare-hex rule governs our documents; an
OCI digest keeps the spelling its own ecosystem uses.
ADR-019 asks for an exact `=version` pin per package. A snapshot timestamp reaches the same
determinism by a stronger route -- it fixes the entire archive the resolver sees, so
transitive dependencies are pinned too, which top-level `=version` pins do not achieve.
`resolved_versions` is MEASURED: dpkg-query run inside the built image, so it is the bill of
materials the image actually has rather than a list somebody maintained. 108 packages,
arch-qualified where dpkg qualifies them. glibc is 2.36, which is what the `bsk` abi3
The interpreter is uv's, not the base image's (ADR-019 decision 1, ADR-014).
`uv_lock` is the SHA-256 of uv.lock, and it appears inside the predicate as uv_lock_sha256 --
which is what makes the predicate pin the dependency set rather than merely describe it.

measurement_status.measured_by: the `container` CI job (GitHub Actions, ubuntu-latest, podman 4.9.3)
measurement_status.reproducibility: two builds, the second --no-cache, produced byte-identical documents
regolded_because: DEV-25: the document is now an ADR-001 envelope at numeric_environment/2, and CPU
capability (`isa_enabled_features`) moved to the unhashed provenance half. It was
refusing environments that computed identical numbers -- two runners differing in that
field and nothing else produced byte-identical channel hashes.
The value was measured by the run above and recomputed from that run's archived
artifact. The property was then checked against real data rather than asserted: the
OTHER machine's 38-feature capability list, grafted into this document's provenance,
leaves the predicate at ce87e66f unchanged.
what_is_still_not_claimed: that this predicate has been OBSERVED equal on two machines: it has been shown invariant under the other machine's recorded capability list, which is the property that matters, but no second runner has yet built at numeric_environment/2

that the ISA pin CHANGES anything: every run since the fix landed on silicon that selects X86_V3 with or without it. NumPy accepts the names -- it rejected the previous six -- and the gate refuses if the selection ever rises above the declared baseline
any cross-CPU claim about the geometry beyond the two shapes compared in DEV-25: one design, four channels, and the X86_V4 runner never produced channel hashes
any cross-OS claim: ADR-006 forecloses one, and `mapped_libraries` refuses off Linux
that DEV-23 is affected. glibc's libm is the path SPICE geometry uses, no ISA pin reaches it, and a narrower predicate makes such a mismatch reachable rather than gone

accepted_image_digests_note: Deliberately empty, and NOT an omission. ADR-019 decision 2: 'a container cannot reliably
read its own image digest from inside', so whatever a runtime injects is a value the operator
asserted. The record therefore treats it as `source: reported` provenance whose mismatch 'is
reported and does not refuse' -- while the PREDICATE, which is measured in-process, is what
